title: Private Continuing Education and Training Centres' Contribution to SkillsFuture Initiatives
what_it_is: Private Continuing Education and Training Centres' Contribution to SkillsFuture Initiatives

sections.label: Private CET Centres and SkillsFuture
sections.summary: Asks how private CET Centres contribute to SkillsFuture and whether Earn and Learn Programmes will expand beyond Polytechnics and ITE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: asked	the Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (a) how are private Continuing Education and Training (CET) Centres contributing to SkillsFuture 	Page: 44 initiatives; and (b) whether there are plans to expand Earn and Learn Programmes to private CET Centres beyond Polytechnics and Institutes of Technical Education.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: There is significance in this change with regard to our understanding of SkillsFuture and it is this: the work done by WDA on Continuing Education and Training and, before that, the Skills Redevelopment Programme, provided the foundation for SkillsFuture today.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It was WDA which set up the CET Centres, funded and supported them, made them publicly accessible, so that workers are empowered to sign up for training and benefit from Government subsidy directly.

sections.label: CET Centres delivering Earn and Learn
sections.summary: CET Centres can deliver Earn and Learn Programmes if capable, willing and industry-supported, with branding aligned to ELPs.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: From a policy perspective, CET Centres can deliver the SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programmes (ELPs) so long as they have the capability and willingness to do so and the industry recognises and supports the programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Centres, such as SEED and the Lithan Academy, already offer work-study training programmes that predate and are broadly similar to the ELPs in terms of funding, delivery, structure and industry acceptance.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They are designed to help mid-career individuals and include features tailored to facilitating career switches.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I will be happy to align the branding of these programmes with the ELPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We started maybe 10-12 years ago with one or two CET Centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This year, we are aiming for 20 ELPs.

sections.label: CET Centres for vulnerable workers
sections.summary: A new phase with older PMEs or vulnerable workers needing help would require setting up CET Centres and ELPs for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Should we enter a new phase where we have older PMEs or other vulnerable workers that require help, certainly, we have to set up CET Centres and ELPs that will cater to their needs.

sections.label: Ascott hotel industry training
sections.summary: Ascott has been providing training for the entire hotel industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For example, Ascott has been providing training for the entire hotel industry.
